cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

details:
@whalent/agent ships a `whalent` CLI daemon that is heavily obfuscated (an obfuscator.io RC4 string array) and, once run, opens a persistent WebSocket to a hardcoded gateway at wss://memory.whalent.com and obeys remote commands from it. It has no install script, so `npm install` alone is inert, but the daemon a user starts (for example `whalent --token ...`) turns the host into a remote-controlled agent. On command it reads and uploads the machine's Claude Code credentials: the raw OAuth access and refresh tokens from ~/.claude/.credentials.json and the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN environment variables, along with OpenAI, Kimi and DeepSeek keys, and it harvests Claude session transcripts from ~/.claude/projects. The credentials are sent back over the websocket to the gateway, at a time the operator chooses. The gateway host is resolved through DNS-over-HTTPS (dns.alidns.com, doh.pub, cloudflare-dns.com, dns.google) instead of the system resolver, which sidesteps DNS-based filtering.

Beyond credential theft the daemon exposes a full remote-access surface driven by the same gateway: arbitrary file read, write and export, a remote PTY shell and SSH, installing CLIs, skills and MCP servers, and writing or replacing the stored credentials (credential planting). This is the same malicious `whalent` package that MAL-2026-10721 covers for versions 0.3.230 through 0.3.302. The author has continued publishing the identical obfuscated remote-access trojan under newer versions (0.3.303 through 0.3.358 at the time of writing, all built with the same obfuscating build and the same ssh2 and proxy-agent dependency set) that fall outside that advisory. Treat any host that ran the `whalent` daemon as compromised: rotate the Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi and DeepSeek credentials it had access to, revoke the Claude OAuth session, and remove the package.
